## phenix vm capture list

List the running packet captures of an experiment or a VM

### Synopsis

```text
List the running packet captures of an experiment or a VM

  Prints the VM, the interface index and the file of each running packet
  capture. With a VM name, the table shows only the captures of that VM. A
  stopped experiment has no captures. -o json and -o yaml print the
  captures with the fields of GET /experiments/{name}/captures.
```

```text
phenix vm capture list <experiment name> [<vm name>] [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix vm capture list my-exp
phenix vm capture list my-exp web -o json
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help            help for list
  -o, --output string   Output format (table, json, yaml) (default "table")
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm capture](vm.md#phenix-vm-capture) - Modify network packet captures for one or more VMs

## phenix vm capture stream

Write a running packet capture to stdout as it is captured

### Synopsis

```text
Write a running packet capture to stdout as it is captured

  Writes the capture as a pcap stream: every packet captured so far (or, with
  --from-now, none of them), then each packet as it is captured, until the
  capture stops or the command is interrupted. Pipe it into Wireshark to
  watch it live:

    phenix vm capture stream <exp> <vm> <iface> | wireshark -k -i -
```

```text
phenix vm capture stream <experiment name> <vm name> <iface name/index> [flags]
```

### Options

```text
      --from-now             Skip the packets captured before the command started
  -h, --help                 help for stream
  -O, --output-file string   Write the capture to this file instead of stdout
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm capture](vm.md#phenix-vm-capture) - Modify network packet captures for one or more VMs

## phenix vm commit

Create a backing image from the disk of a running VM

### Synopsis

```text
Create a backing image from the disk of a running VM

  Writes the first disk of the VM as it is now, with the changes in its
  snapshot, to a new image that has no backing image. phenix shuts down the
  VM while it writes the image, and then starts the VM again. It also starts
  the VM again if the operation fails.

  The image name must be a bare file name, with no folder. Without an image
  name, phenix names the image after the base image of the VM and the time,
  for example ubuntu_20261106120000.qc2. phenix writes the image in
  <base-dir.phenix>/images on the head node, copies it to the other cluster
  nodes, and prints its name. The VM can run on any cluster node.

  The experiment and the VM must run, and the VM must have its snapshot flag
  set. For a VM with more than one disk, the image holds only the first disk.
  The other disks do not change.
```

```text
phenix vm commit <experiment name> <vm name> [image name] [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix vm commit my-exp web web-configured.qc2
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help   help for commit
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm](vm.md) - Virtual machine management

## phenix vm cp

Copy a file into or out of a running VM

### Synopsis

```text
Copy a file into or out of a running VM

  Copy one file between the local host and a running VM through the VM's
  miniccc agent, as scp does. Name the VM side as <vm name>:<path>, with an
  absolute path in the VM. Exactly one of <src> and <dst> must name the VM.
  A path that ends with "/" is a folder, and the file keeps its name.

  To copy into the VM, phenix puts a staging copy in the experiment's folder
  of the minimega files directory. It sends the copy with "cc send" and then
  moves it to the path in the VM. To copy out of the VM, phenix gets the file
  with "cc recv". This works only for a VM on the headnode, and for a Unix
  path with no glob characters. phenix removes the staging copy and the
  received copy when the copy is complete. A file copied out of the VM gets
  the permissions 0600. The VM must run the miniccc agent.
```

```text
phenix vm cp <experiment name> <src> <dst> [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix vm cp myexp ./setup.sh host-01:/root/setup.sh
phenix vm cp myexp ./setup.sh host-01:/root/
phenix vm cp myexp host-01:/var/log/syslog ./syslog
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help               help for cp
      --timeout duration   How long to wait for the VM to complete the copy (default 1m0s)
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm](vm.md) - Virtual machine management

## phenix vm exec

Run a command in a running VM

### Synopsis

```text
Run a command in a running VM

  Run a command in a running VM through its miniccc agent, as the minimega
  command "cc exec" does, and print the stdout and stderr of the command.
  The command exits with the exit code of the command in the VM when minimega
  reports it.

  miniccc runs the command without a shell. To use pipes or redirects, run a
  shell, such as "sh -c '...'". Put "--" before a command that has flags.
  phenix refuses an argument that minimega would change on the host: an
  argument with a "$" variable, or a file:, http:, https: or tar: URL. The VM
  must run the miniccc agent.
```

```text
phenix vm exec <experiment name> <vm name> [--] <command> [args...] [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix vm exec myexp host-01 hostname
phenix vm exec myexp host-01 --timeout 5m -- ls -la /tmp
phenix vm exec myexp host-01 -- sh -c 'ps aux | grep nginx'
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help               help for exec
      --timeout duration   How long to wait for the command to complete (default 1m0s)
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm](vm.md) - Virtual machine management

## phenix vm forward

List, add, or remove the port forwards of a VM

### Synopsis

```text
List, add, or remove the port forwards of a VM

  A port forward is a minimega tunnel from a cluster port to a port that the
  VM reaches, which phenix-tunneler serves on the computer of its owner. The
  running phenix server holds the forwards, so these commands call it over
  its unix socket (--unix-socket). The server takes a request from the socket
  as the user global-admin, so a forward that the CLI adds has that owner,
  and the CLI removes only the forwards of that owner.
```

```text
phenix vm forward [flags]
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help   help for forward
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm](vm.md) - Virtual machine management
* [phenix vm forward add](vm.md#phenix-vm-forward-add) - Add a port forward to a VM
* [phenix vm forward list](vm.md#phenix-vm-forward-list) - List the port forwards of a VM
* [phenix vm forward remove](vm.md#phenix-vm-forward-remove) - Remove a port forward of a VM

## phenix vm forward add

Add a port forward to a VM

### Synopsis

```text
Add a port forward to a VM

  Opens a minimega tunnel from a cluster port to the destination port on
  --host, as the cluster node of the VM reaches it. With vnc, the forward
  goes to the VNC console of the VM. --source-port is the port that
  phenix-tunneler listens on; it defaults to the destination port. An owner
  has at most one forward to each host and port of a VM.
```

```text
phenix vm forward add <experiment name> <vm name> <destination port|vnc> [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix vm forward add my-exp web 22
phenix vm forward add my-exp web 80 --host 10.0.0.5 --source-port 8080
phenix vm forward add my-exp web vnc
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help                 help for add
      --host string          Destination host, as the cluster node of the VM reaches it (default "127.0.0.1")
      --source-port string   Port for phenix-tunneler to listen on (default the destination port)
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm forward](vm.md#phenix-vm-forward) - List, add, or remove the port forwards of a VM

## phenix vm info

Table of virtual machine(s)

### Synopsis

```text
Table of VM(s)

  Used to display a table of virtual machine(s) for a specific experiment;
  VM name is optional, when included will display only that VM.

  Filter the output by repeating --filter with a COLUMN=VALUE expression.
  Multiple filters are combined with AND semantics. Column names and values
  are case-insensitive. Supported columns are HOST, NAME, RUNNING, DISK,
  INTERFACES, UPTIME, MEMORY, VCPUS, OS_TYPE, and TAPS. DISK values may be
  full paths, filenames, or filenames without extensions. For example:

    phenix vm info my-experiment --filter RUNNING=true
    phenix vm info my-experiment --filter RUNNING=true --filter OS_TYPE=linux
    phenix vm info my-experiment --filter DISK=jammy

  Repeat --host to list only the VMs running on any of the named cluster
  hosts, named exactly as minimega reports them. --host combines with the VM
  name or --label, and with --filter: a VM must match each of them. For
  example:

    phenix vm info my-experiment --host compute1 --host compute2
    phenix vm info my-experiment --host compute1 --label role-web

  -o json and -o yaml print each VM with the fields of the API, as
  GET /experiments/{exp}/vms gives them.
```

```text
phenix vm info <experiment name> [vm name] [flags]
```

### Options

```text
  -f, --filter stringArray   Filter output by column value (COLUMN=VALUE); may be repeated
  -h, --help                 help for info
      --host stringArray     Cluster host to filter VMs by, named exactly as minimega reports it; may be repeated
  -l, --label stringArray    Label to filter VMs (supports glob patterns); use 'all' to select every VM
  -o, --output string        Output format (table, json, yaml) (default "table")
  -t, --taps                 Include tap interface names in the table
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm](vm.md) - Virtual machine management

## phenix vm mount

Mount a VM's filesystem on the headnode

```text
Mount a VM's filesystem on the headnode

  Mount the filesystem of a running virtual machine to a directory on the
```

## phenix vm qos

View or change the link quality of VM interfaces

### Synopsis

```text
View or change the link quality of VM interfaces

  The link quality is the packet loss, the delay or the rate limit that
  minimega applies to the traffic that a VM interface receives. A rate cannot
  go with a loss or a delay. The experiment must run. An interface is an
  index from 0 or an interface name of the topology.
```

```text
phenix vm qos [flags]
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help   help for qos
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm](vm.md) - Virtual machine management
* [phenix vm qos clear](vm.md#phenix-vm-qos-clear) - Remove the link quality of a VM interface, or of all its interfaces
* [phenix vm qos get](vm.md#phenix-vm-qos-get) - Show the link quality of each interface of a VM
* [phenix vm qos set](vm.md#phenix-vm-qos-set) - Replace the link quality of a VM interface

## phenix vm qos clear

Remove the link quality of a VM interface, or of all its interfaces

### Synopsis

```text
Remove the link quality of a VM interface, or of all its interfaces

  With an interface, removes the link quality of that interface. Without one,
  removes the link quality of each interface that has one.
```

```text
phenix vm qos clear <experiment name> <vm name> [<interface>] [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix vm qos clear my-exp web 0
phenix vm qos clear my-exp web
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help   help for clear
```

## phenix vm qos set

Replace the link quality of a VM interface

### Synopsis

```text
Replace the link quality of a VM interface

  Clears the link quality of the interface, then applies each setting given.
  Give a --loss, a --delay or both, or give a --rate alone.
```

```text
phenix vm qos set <experiment name> <vm name> <interface> [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix vm qos set my-exp web 0 --loss 0.5 --delay 100ms
phenix vm qos set my-exp web IF0 --rate 10mbit
```

### Options

```text
      --delay string   Delay to add to each packet, in us, ms or s, such as 100ms
  -h, --help           help for set
      --loss string    Percent of packets to drop, from 0 up to 100, such as 0.5
      --rate string    Rate limit, a whole number of kbit, mbit or gbit, such as 10mbit
```

## phenix vm redeploy

Redeploy running experiment VM(s)

### Synopsis

```text
Redeploy running experiment VM(s)

  Used to redeploy running virtual machine(s) for a specific experiment; several redeploy
  values can be modified. The CPU and memory values change only when their flags are set.
  A new disk replaces only the first disk of the VM. The disk value is
  <path>[,<interface>][,<cache>]; a field that the value leaves out keeps the value of
  the old first disk.
```

```text
phenix vm redeploy <experiment name> [vm name] [flags]
```

### Options

```text
  -c, --cpu int             Number of VM CPUs (1-8 is valid; 0 keeps the current value)
  -d, --disk string         New first disk: <path>[,<interface>][,<cache>]
  -h, --help                help for redeploy
  -l, --label stringArray   Label to filter VMs (supports glob patterns); use 'all' to select every VM
  -m, --mem int             Amount of memory in megabytes (a multiple of 512 from 512 to 16384; 0 keeps the current value)
  -p, --partition int       Partition of the new disk to inject files into (used only with --disk and --replicate-injects) (default 1)
  -r, --replicate-injects   Recreate disk snapshot and VM injections
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm](vm.md) - Virtual machine management

## phenix vm screenshot

Save a screenshot of the screen of a running VM

### Synopsis

```text
Save a screenshot of the screen of a running VM

  Writes the screen of the VM as a PNG image to the --output-file file, or to
  stdout when stdout is not a terminal. With --size, minimega scales the
  image so that its longest side is at most that many pixels. The experiment
  must run.

```


## phenix vm set

Set configuration value(s) for VM(s)

### Synopsis

```text
Set configuration value(s) for VM(s)

  Used to set one or more configuration values for virtual machine(s) in an
  experiment. Only flags that are explicitly provided will be applied.

  While the experiment is running, you can change only the labels
  (--label-changes, --append-labels), the annotations (--annotation) and the
  VLAN of an interface (--interface). Apps read the new annotations when the
  experiment starts again. --interface changes only a VM of a running
  experiment.

  --annotation replaces all of the annotations of the VM with the given ones.
  The values true and false become booleans, and a JSON list or object keeps
  its type. Other values, numbers too, stay text.

  --interface <index>=<vlan> connects the interface with that index to a VLAN
  alias or ID. --interface <index>= disconnects the interface.

  --partition 0 turns off disk injection for the VM, so the startup app sends
  its scripts through miniccc.
```

```text
phenix vm set <experiment name> [vm name] [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix vm set <experiment name> <vm name> --cpu 2 --mem 4096
phenix vm set <experiment name> <vm name> --host compute1
phenix vm set <experiment name> <vm name> --annotation phenix/default-apps=false
phenix vm set <experiment name> <vm name> --interface 0=EXP_1
phenix vm set <experiment name> <vm name> --interface 1=
phenix vm set <experiment name> --label role=server --label-changes tier=web --append-labels
```

### Options

```text
      --annotation stringArray      VM annotation in key=value form (may be repeated; replaces all of the annotations of the VM)
      --append-labels               Append the provided labels to the VM's existing labels instead of replacing the labels
  -c, --cpu int                     Number of VM CPUs (1-8 is valid)
  -d, --disk string                 VM backing disk image file
      --do-not-boot                 Set the do-not-boot flag for the VM
  -h, --help                        help for set
      --host string                 Cluster host to run the VM on (an empty value lets the scheduler choose the host)
      --interface string            Connect an interface to a VLAN alias or ID as <index>=<vlan>, or disconnect it as <index>= (running experiments only)
  -l, --label stringArray           Label to filter VMs (supports glob patterns); use 'all' to select every VM
  -L, --label-changes stringArray   VM label(s) to add or edit in key=value form (may be repeated)
  -m, --mem int                     Amount of memory in megabytes (a multiple of 512 from 512 to 16384)
  -p, --partition int               Partition of the first disk to inject files into (0 turns off disk injection)
      --snapshot                    Set the snapshot (non-persistent) flag for the VM
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm](vm.md) - Virtual machine management

## phenix vm snapshot

List, create, restore, and delete VM disk and memory snapshots

### Synopsis

```text
List, create, restore, and delete the snapshots of a VM

  A snapshot holds the disk and the memory state of a VM in a running
  experiment. Restore a snapshot to return the VM to that state. For an ELF
  memory dump, use phenix vm memory-snapshot.

  To create or restore a snapshot, the VM must have its snapshot flag set and
  exactly one disk. phenix refuses a VM with more than one disk, because a
  snapshot holds only the first disk (sandialabs/sceptre-phenix#145).

  phenix keeps the snapshot files on the cluster node that runs the VM, in
  <base-dir.phenix>/images/<experiment name>/files. The list shows the
  snapshots on all nodes. A restore of a VM on a node other than the head
  node can fail if minimega on that node runs with the -headnode flag:
  minimega then gets the snapshot files from the head node, which does not
  have them (sandialabs/sceptre-phenix#153).
```

```text
phenix vm snapshot [flags]
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help   help for snapshot
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm](vm.md) - Virtual machine management
* [phenix vm snapshot create](vm.md#phenix-vm-snapshot-create) - Create a snapshot of a running VM
* [phenix vm snapshot delete](vm.md#phenix-vm-snapshot-delete) - Delete one of the snapshots of a VM
* [phenix vm snapshot list](vm.md#phenix-vm-snapshot-list) - List the snapshots of a VM
* [phenix vm snapshot restore](vm.md#phenix-vm-snapshot-restore) - Restore a VM to one of its snapshots

## phenix vm snapshot create

Create a snapshot of a running VM

### Synopsis

```text
Create a snapshot of a running VM

  Saves the disk and the memory state of the VM as a snapshot. The snapshot
  name must be a bare file name, with no folder. phenix removes an extension
  from the name, and names the snapshot <vm name>__<snapshot name>. The
  command prints that name.

  minimega pauses the VM while it saves the snapshot, and then resumes the VM.
  The command waits up to one hour for the save. The experiment and the VM
  must run.
```

```text
phenix vm snapshot create <experiment name> <vm name> <snapshot name> [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix vm snapshot create my-exp web before-update
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help   help for create
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm snapshot](vm.md#phenix-vm-snapshot) - List, create, restore, and delete VM disk and memory snapshots

## phenix vm snapshot delete

Delete one of the snapshots of a VM

### Synopsis

```text
Delete one of the snapshots of a VM

  Deletes the memory state and the disk of the snapshot from the experiment's
  files directory on every cluster node. Give the snapshot name as phenix vm
  snapshot list prints it. The experiment does not have to run. phenix
  refuses a snapshot whose disk a running VM uses, as it does after a
  restore.
```

```text
phenix vm snapshot delete <experiment name> <vm name> <snapshot name> [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix vm snapshot delete my-exp web web__before-update
```

### Options

```text
      --dry-run   Show what the command would change, and change nothing
  -h, --help      help for delete
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm snapshot](vm.md#phenix-vm-snapshot) - List, create, restore, and delete VM disk and memory snapshots

```text
  experiment does not have to run. -o json and -o yaml print the names as a
  list.
```

```text

```


## phenix vm snapshot restore

Restore a VM to one of its snapshots

### Synopsis

```text
Restore a VM to one of its snapshots

  Relaunches the VM from the disk and the memory state of the snapshot. The
  VM keeps its UUID. The VM loses all changes made after the snapshot. Give
  the snapshot name as phenix vm snapshot list prints it. The experiment must
  run.
```

```text
phenix vm snapshot restore <experiment name> <vm name> <snapshot name> [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix vm snapshot restore my-exp web web__before-update
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help   help for restore
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix vm snapshot](vm.md#phenix-vm-snapshot) - List, create, restore, and delete VM disk and memory snapshots
